scenes.headline: How MiniMax Music 3 writes a whole song
scenes.sub: An 8B planner, a 646M detailer, and flow matching to 32 kHz stereo.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Biscuit! MiniMax Music 3 turns lyrics and a description into a complete song, up to five minutes long. Here's how the work is split.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A big LLM writes the song's structure one token per frame, a small one adds texture, and synthesis renders their hidden states, not tokens.
scenes.say: A big model writes the song's structure, one token per frame. A small one adds the texture. And the sound is rendered from their hidden states, not their tokens.

steps.say: The Global LLM, eight billion parameters, reads the lyrics and description and commits one semantic token per frame. That token carries the structure.
A small Local LLM fills in the other seven codebooks inside each frame. That's the texture.
Here's the unusual part. Synthesis doesn't decode those tokens. It fuses the final hidden states of both models.
Flow matching works from there, and a Flow-VAE decoder turns it into stereo audio.

steps.note: the tokenizer is a training-time device
steps.say: So the tokens shape what the models learn to predict, and are then bypassed.

scenes.title: What one frame costs
scenes.say: How much does the model actually predict?

parts.say: Fourteen bits for the semantic token.
Ten each for the seven acoustic ones.
Eighty-four bits a frame. At thirty frames a second, two point five two kilobits a second.

scenes.label: is five minutes of song, where the card's two ceilings agree
scenes.note: raw 32 kHz stereo PCM would be 1,024 kbit/s
scenes.say: So a five-minute song is nine thousand steps. The card gives both limits, but never says thirty frames a second. That's where they meet.

scenes.label: Card parameter counts that match the files
scenes.note: the global LLM is Qwen3-8B, vocabulary widened to 200,000
scenes.say: All four parameter counts on the card match the bytes on disk. The global model is exactly Qwen3-8B, with a wider vocabulary for the music tokens.

scenes.text: The tokens are what the models predict; the hidden states are what actually gets rendered.
scenes.say: The tokens are what the models predict. The hidden states are what actually gets rendered.

recap: An 8B model plans, a 646M one adds texture
84 bits a frame, 9,000 frames a song
Sound comes from hidden states, not tokens
scenes.say: To recap: a planner and a detailer, eighty-four bits a frame, and sound rendered from hidden states.
